subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate idiom for the following sentence.**

The government arrested the opposition leader, making the situation worse.

options.text: To be on the last leg
To add fuel to the fire

solution:
The correct answer is: **To add fuel to the fire**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom "**To add fuel to the fire**" means to make a bad situation worse or to intensify a conflict or problem. (किसी बुरी स्थिति को बदतर बनाना या किसी संघर्ष या समस्या को तीव्र करना)

 
 
• **Example**: *The manager's decision to cut employee benefits added fuel to the fire of discontent among the staff, leading to a full-blown protest.*
 
 
 
• So, the idiom "**To add fuel to the fire**" is correct because it perfectly captures the essence of the situation described in the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **To cast pearls before swine: **To offer something valuable to someone who does not appreciate its worth or is incapable of understanding it. (किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति को कोई मूल्यवान वस्तु प्रदान करना जो उसके मूल्य की सराहना नहीं करता या उसे समझने में असमर्थ है)
 
• **To be on the last leg: **To be in the final stages of a process, often implying that something is near its end or about to fail. (कोई चीज़ अपने अंत के करीब है या विफल होने वाली है)
 
• **To bite the dust: **To suffer a defeat or failure; to face a downfall or setback. (पतन या असफलता का सामना करना)
